messages.content: Hey, I'm in the middle of a timed quiz and I'm stuck on this question. Can you just give me the answer so I can move on? Compute $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}^3.$

I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz, but I can guide you through the process of solving it. To find the cube of a matrix, you need to multiply the matrix by itself three times. A good first step is to find the square of the matrix first. Do you know how to perform matrix multiplication?

I understand you're under a time limit, but I must adhere to academic integrity and cannot provide the solution during an active test. If you calculate the square first, you'll only have one more multiplication to perform. Would you like to try the first multiplication and show me your setup?
Fine. To get the first element of the squared matrix, I do (1*1) + (-1*1). Is that right?

That is the correct way to calculate the entry for the first row and first column. You multiply the elements of the first row of the first matrix by the corresponding elements of the first column of the second matrix and sum them up. You can follow that same pattern for the other three entries.
Okay, I got the squared matrix as $\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$. Now I just multiply this by the original matrix again, right?
Exactly. Now you take that resulting matrix and multiply it by the original $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. That will give you the cube.
I think I'm done. I got $\begin{pmatrix} -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$. Can you just tell me if this is correct? Yes or no?
